records.title: PERF-01 — Representative benchmark fixtures
records.body:
## Context

Every performance ticket in this milestone needs data to run against, and "representative" is the load-bearing word. A benchmark over 100 flat contacts measures nothing that matters: the operations that get slow here are relationship traversal on a dense graph, FTS over a large corpus, and export over contacts with many repeatable fields — none of which appear in a thin dataset.

There is prior art to build on rather than duplicate: `backend/controllers/hot_paths_perf_test.go`, `backend/services/reach_out_trigger_perf_test.go`, and `backend/cmd/loadsmoke`, which fires parallel writes at a running instance to catch `SQLITE_BUSY` and rate-limit regressions against the real deployed artifact (issue #262).

This should also be one dataset generator, not three. #495 (large-dataset migration) and #498 (constrained resources) need the same thing, and three independent notions of "big" would make their results incomparable.

## Recommended actions

1. Define the scale profiles as written numbers, and keep them few. Two or three is enough:
   - **typical** — what a real personal-CRM user has after a few years
   - **large** — a heavy user, or someone who imported an entire address book history
   - **stress** — beyond intended MVP scale, to find the cliff rather than to promise support
   State contacts, relationships per contact (including a few hubs — the graph is not uniform, and traversal cost lives in the tails), notes, activities, life events, attachments and their total size, resulting database size, **and user count** — multi-user is supported at `1.0.0` (#558), and per-user jobs and indexes scale with it independently of per-user data volume.
2. Generate by scaling the TEST-02 manifest (#430), so pathological records exist at every scale rather than only plain ones. The slow query is usually the one hitting the contact with forty phone numbers.
3. Make generation deterministic and seeded, so a regression is reproducible and two runs are comparable.
4. Make it fast enough to be usable, and cache the generated database as a CI artifact rather than rebuilding a large dataset on every run.
5. Include the shapes that break specific subsystems: deep relationship chains and dense hubs for traversal, a large text corpus for FTS, many attachments for storage and backup, and Unicode-heavy content for tokenizer behavior.
6. Publish the profiles as the documented resource requirements the milestone asks for, so an operator can size a deployment.

## How to verify

- Profiles are documented with concrete numbers and a rationale.
- Generation is deterministic from a seed.
- The same generator serves #469, #470, #495, and #498 — assert that by using it, not by intending to.
- The generated dataset passes DB-01's invariant checks (#460) — a fixture that violates invariants would make every downstream measurement meaningless.
- Generating the large profile completes in a time that keeps CI usable, and the result is cached.

## Notes

Milestone `v0.6.9`. Depends on #430 (TEST-02 manifest). Consumed by #469 (PERF-02), #470 (PERF-03), #471 (PERF-04), #495 (migration at scale), #498 (constrained resources), #453 (restore at scale). Existing: `backend/controllers/hot_paths_perf_test.go`, `backend/services/reach_out_trigger_perf_test.go`, `backend/cmd/loadsmoke` (issue #262). Gate: #539.

records.title: Recursive CTE support: WithRecursive API, WITH RECURSIVE dialect gating, CTE self-reference binding
records.body:
## Summary

Recursive CTEs are not supported and are **not expressible** through the current API. There is no `RECURSIVE` token anywhere in the codebase — not in the generator, the runtime, the shared SQL parser, or the dialect config. This is an absence rather than a defect: users have no way to write one, so nothing silently mis-compiles today.

This issue tracks implementing the full `WithRecursive` feature as designed below.

## Current state

Non-recursive CTEs are largely complete, and a meaningful amount of the required machinery already exists:

| Existing capability | Location |
|---|---|
| `CteDef` / `CteColumn` IR (inner SQL, DTO-derived columns, carrier parameter offset) | `src/Quarry.Generator/IR/CteDef.cs` |
| `WITH "x" AS (…)` rendering (three call sites) | `src/Quarry.Generator/IR/SqlAssembler.cs:216`, `:426`, `:1614` |
| Inner-plan re-render with rebased parameter offset (multi-CTE `@p0` collision fix) | `SqlAssembler.cs:243-256` |
| CTE definition/resolution, QRY080/081/082 | `src/Quarry.Generator/Parsing/ChainAnalyzer.cs:754-987` |
| DTO column resolution | `src/Quarry.Generator/IR/CteDtoResolver.cs`, called from `UsageSiteDiscovery.cs:3883-3885` |
| Runtime stubs (`With<TDto>`, `With<TEntity,TDto>`, `FromCte<TDto>`) | `src/Quarry/Context/QuarryContext.cs:150`, `:164`, `:174`; `QuarryContext<TSelf>` overrides at `:644`, `:652` |
| CTE→CTE joins (`FromCte<A>().Join<B>(…)`) | existing, covered by tests |
| Set operations render inline inside a CTE body | `SqlAssembler.cs:287-299` |

That last row matters: `UNION ALL` inside a CTE body is essentially free — the operand rendering path is already recursive over `QueryPlan`.

## Blockers

### 1. No way to self-reference the CTE (the dominant cost)

The recursive member needs `FROM cte JOIN base ON …`. Two things prevent it:

- The `With` lambda is `Func<IEntityAccessor<TDto>, IQueryBuilder<TDto>>` — there is no handle on the CTE currently being defined.
- `FromCte<TDto>()` resolution iterates **forward** and requires a matching `CteDef` to already exist in the list, otherwise it emits QRY081 (`ChainAnalyzer.cs:962-986`). A self-reference violates that ordering by construction.

Work required: a new entry point, a new `InterceptorKind`, discovery wiring in `UsageSiteDiscovery` (the `With`/`FromCte` dispatch is name-based at `UsageSiteDiscovery.cs:3871`), and a binder path where the chain root is a CTE rather than a schema entity. `CallSiteBinder.cs:126-134` already carries a "DTO is not a schema entity" fallback for CTE chains — that is the hook — but column binding against `CteDef.Columns` instead of `EntityInfo` is new code.

### 2. `WITH RECURSIVE` keyword + dialect gating

`"WITH "` is a hardcoded string literal at all three `SqlAssembler` sites listed above. PostgreSQL, SQLite, and MySQL 8+ require `WITH RECURSIVE`; SQL Server forbids the keyword entirely. The keyword is per-`WITH`-clause, not per-CTE, so the flag belongs on the plan (or is derived as "any `CteDef.IsRecursive`"), plus a capability on `SqlDialectConfig` (`src/Quarry.Generator/Sql/SqlDialectConfig.cs`). MySQL 8.0 minimum is not knowable at compile time — document it.

Small: roughly 50 LOC plus the config field.

### 3. CTE bodies emit no column aliases

Current output (`src/Quarry.Tests/SqlOutput/CrossDialectCteTests.cs:40`):

```sql
WITH "Order" AS (SELECT "OrderId", "UserId", "Total", … FROM "orders" WHERE "Total" > 100)
SELECT "OrderId", "Total" FROM "Order"
```

This works only because DTO property names happen to coincide with column names. Recursive members compute values (`n.Depth + 1`, path concatenation) that have no natural column name, and the anchor and recursive members must produce identically-named columns.

Recommended fix: emit an explicit column list — `WITH RECURSIVE "cte"("A","B") AS (…)`. One loop over `CteDef.Columns`, valid on all four dialects, and simpler than retrofitting `AS` alias emission into the projection renderer.

### 4. Recursion-specific semantics

- SQL Server defaults to `MAXRECURSION 100` and hard-errors past it. The escape hatch is `OPTION (MAXRECURSION n)`, which **must be the final clause** of the outer statement — this interacts with pagination and `Prepare()` render ordering.
- Validation the engines require anyway, surfaced as compile-time diagnostics instead of runtime errors: recursive member references the CTE exactly once; no aggregates / `DISTINCT` / `ORDER BY` / `LIMIT` in the recursive member; no outer join to the CTE; anchor member may not reference the CTE.

## Proposed API

```csharp
public class EmployeeSchema : Schema
{
    public static string Table => "employees";
    public Key<int> EmployeeId => Identity();
    public Col<string> Name => Length(100);
    public Ref<EmployeeSchema, int?> ManagerId => ForeignKey<EmployeeSchema, int?>();
}

public record EmployeeNode(int EmployeeId, string Name, int Depth);
```

records.title: Make web skill discovery recursive, matching the CLI
records.body:
## Problem

The CLI and the web app use different rules to discover skills.

The CLI scans skill directories recursively and follows directory symlinks. The web skill library checks only this path:

```text
<skill-root>/<direct-child>/SKILL.md
```

This difference prevents the web app and rooms from finding skills inside a repository-level symlink.

## Example

```text
~/.agents/skills/agent-skills -> ~/Projekte/agent-skills
~/Projekte/agent-skills/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md
```

With this structure:

- The CLI finds 72 skills.
- The web API finds 24 direct skills.
- The web app misses 48 skills below the `agent-skills` symlink.

A symlink that points directly to one skill works. A symlink that points to a repository or collection does not work.

## Expected behavior

The CLI, web skill library, and rooms should use the same recursive discovery rules. This behavior also matches Pi, Claude Code, and Codex.

## Current implementation

The CLI loader recursively calls `loadSkillsFromDirInternal()` and resolves symlinks with `realPath()`:

```text
runtime/packages/agent/src/harness/skills.ts
```

The web library reads only direct children and checks `path.join(dir, entry.name, "SKILL.md")`:

```text
apps/web-server/src/index.ts
```

The current symlink test covers only a direct symlink to one skill. It does not cover a symlink to a directory that contains several skills:

```text
apps/web-server/scripts/skills-shared-dir-smoke.ts
```

I reproduced the API result locally with v0.8.0. The same non-recursive web discovery code is present in v0.10.1 (`2963a17d9d4b58581d94a8b954511a5c04bb870a`).

## Suggested change

Use the recursive runtime discovery rules for the web skill library and room skill resolution.

Please keep these existing rules:

- Skip dot directories and `node_modules`.
- Honor ignore files.
- Keep the current source precedence.
- Prevent loops when symlinks point back to a parent directory.
- Use the same resolved manifest path for listing, enabling, and fingerprint checks.

## Acceptance criteria

- The web library finds skills in nested directories.
- The web library follows a symlink to a repository or skill collection.
- Direct skill symlinks continue to work.
- The CLI and web app list the same skills for the same configured roots.
- A symlink loop does not hang the scan.

records.title: Detect circular dependencies
records.body:
Extend the topological sort to detect circular dependencies. When a cycle is found, produce an error that names every contract in the cycle in traversal order. The detection must find all cycles, not just the first one. This runs during `build()` before any deployment happens.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- A cycle A → B → C → A produces an error message containing all three labels in cycle order
- Multiple independent cycles are all reported in a single error
- The error message is human-readable and actionable (not a raw graph dump)
- Unit tests cover: simple cycle (A→B→A), multi-node cycle, multiple independent cycles, cycle in a subgraph of an otherwise valid DAG

**Expectations**
What done looks like: A unified `Config` builder that initializes all networking variables centrally.
For any question, reach me on Discord: emry_ss

records.title: 28.14 — Flux proxies, cache and background processing
records.body:
## Objective

The infrastructure that makes editing large media feasible in a browser: proxies, caches and background jobs.

## Scope

- Proxy media: generation at defined resolutions and codecs, automatic proxy/full switching, proxy status per source, and re-linking to full quality for export.
- Render cache: cached rendered ranges with timeline indication, precise invalidation on any upstream change, size limits and eviction.
- Thumbnail and waveform caches, persistent across sessions (28.3, 28.9).
- Background job system: proxy generation, cache rendering, media analysis, import conversion, export — with progress, cancellation, prioritisation and survival across a mode switch (#98).
- Storage management: cache and proxy storage budgets, visible usage, and user-controlled purge — building on the existing storage-usage reporting.
- Media analysis jobs: scene detection, audio waveform, loudness analysis, where they earn their place.
- Behaviour under quota exhaustion and when the machine is under load.

## Dependencies

- **Depends on:** 24.7 (worker and job architecture), 28.1 (media model), 28.2 (playback quality modes).
- **Blocks:** 28.15, 28.16.

## Technical considerations

- `@ffmpeg/ffmpeg` and `src/workers/video.worker.ts` already exist for conversion; proxy generation should extend that pipeline rather than introduce a second one. Its performance characteristics are already known from the existing conversion work.
- Cache invalidation is the hard part: an edit invalidates a range, an effect change invalidates differently, a source change invalidates everything downstream. Get the dependency model right in 28.1/24.4 and this is tractable.
- Proxy storage on top of source storage doubles disk pressure; the budget and the purge path are not optional.
- Jobs must survive a mode switch, per #98, and must not be lost on a reload without a resume or a clear restart.

## UX requirements

- Proxy and cache status are visible at a glance, on the timeline and per source.
- Storage usage is visible and purgeable, consistent with how the app already reports storage.
- Background jobs are listed with progress and are cancellable individually.
- The app remains fully usable while jobs run.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Proxy generation at defined presets with automatic switching and full-quality relink for export.
- [ ] Render cache with timeline indication, precise invalidation, budgets and eviction.
- [ ] Thumbnail and waveform caches persist across sessions.
- [ ] Job system with progress, cancellation, prioritisation and survival across a mode switch.
- [ ] Storage budgets visible and purgeable; quota exhaustion handled visibly.
- [ ] Proxy pipeline extends the existing video worker rather than duplicating it.
- [ ] The app stays responsive while jobs run, verified under load.

## Testing

Integration: proxy generation and switching; cache invalidation across edit, effect and source changes; job survival across a mode switch. Unit: cache key derivation and eviction. Storage: quota exhaustion path. Benchmark: UI responsiveness under concurrent jobs.

## Out of scope

Encoding for delivery (28.15).



---

Part of **phase 28 — Flux: video & motion** — epic #209. Roadmap: [docs/architecture/creative-suite.md](https://github.com/FraOri03/Lattice/blob/main/docs/architecture/creative-suite.md).

records.title: ROAD MANAGER — Authoritative road-junction and connected-road graph for every pad county
records.body:
## Goal
Make BrineSearch Road Manager understand **physical road connectivity**, not merely road names.

For every drivable/public road in every current BrineSearch pad county in Ohio, West Virginia, and Pennsylvania, Road Manager must be able to answer:

`road identity → every true junction → exact GPS coordinate → every connected road identity → aliases/designations → source/confidence`

This is the durable engineering implementation of the road-intelligence/connectivity research completed in Chat on 2026-08-11.

Parent data issue: #70
Related structured-route consumer: #69
Master workflow: #68

## Current live checkpoint
Start from current `main` `4066834452e1f79ab5a6da967d2576127cada0a6` (PR #96 merged/live NLF consolidation) and current production Supabase before changing anything.

Production at issue creation:
- `brinesearch_roads`: 402 canonical Road Manager rows
- 298 have centerline geometry
- 294 have route-publishable complete geometry
- #70 remains open for unresolved/ambiguous Ohio roads, WV/PA road coverage, mileage, and route readiness
- #69 already has strict Road Manager boundary/snap/clip RPCs and must remain fail-closed/no-guess

Open engineering PR overlap check at issue creation found no active Road Manager feature PR; the visible open PR #34 is a Dependabot Vite update and is unrelated.

## Confirmed county scope
The current research footprint contains **39 confirmed BrineSearch pad counties**:
- Ohio: 19
- West Virginia: 10
- Pennsylvania: 10

Do not blindly trust typed `pads.county` / township spelling. Use the already-established authoritative pad-footprint research and official geographic identifiers. If future pad counties are added, the system must be extendable without redesign.

## Authoritative source hierarchy
### Ohio
Primary: ODOT TIMS / Road Inventory FeatureServer.
Existing production `brinesearch_odot_road_catalog` already contains segment-level ODOT inventory/geometry and must be reused rather than duplicated.

### West Virginia
Primary: WVDOT Enterprise Road Network / Publication LRS plus Street Name DOH/SAMS and alternate route-name events tied to WVDOT `ROUTE_ID` and measures.
Do not assume every WVDOT non-state feature is public/drivable; trails/topology connectors must be classified/held appropriately.

### Pennsylvania
Primary: PennDOT state-road and local-road roadway/LRS layers. Add authoritative county/NG911 centerlines for alias/legacy-name enrichment where available and source-provenanced.
PennDOT internal SR identity, signed traffic route, and local street name are separate identities and must not be collapsed blindly.

TIGER/Line or other public mapping may be used only as supplemental topology/QA evidence, never to override stronger state/county road authority.

## Non-negotiable identity/topology rules
- **Never infer a connection from road-name similarity.**
- A map crossing is not automatically a junction. Reject bridge/overpass crossings unless authoritative topology/ramps show traversability.
- Same-name roads remain separate when geography/source identity differs.
- Same CR number in different counties is not the same road.
- Same TR number in different townships is not automatically the same road.
- WV fractional county routes remain exact identities.
- PennDOT internal SR numbers must not be displayed as signed route numbers unless they actually are signed that way.
- Concurrent/overlapping routes must be represented as multiple identities sharing a physical segment where appropriate.
- Name/route changes through municipalities, townships, counties, and state lines must be preserved as continuation events rather than fake turns.
- A single road may touch another road more than once; every occurrence remains its own junction.
- Multiway junctions must have one physical junction node with all road memberships, not pairwise duplicate fake intersections.
- Shared-segment/overlap geometry must be preserved rather than forced into one point.
- Private/access roads and drivable trails must be classified separately from normal public roads.
- Preserve exact source IDs and provenance.

## Required architecture
Do **not** bulk-inflate `brinesearch_roads` with every raw state/county source segment.

`brinesearch_roads` should remain the canonical BrineSearch route-facing road identity layer.

Build a scalable authoritative source + topology layer underneath it. Exact table/view names may be adjusted after schema review, but the logical model must include:

### 1. Authoritative road source segments
A normalized segment registry/view covering OH/WV/PA source systems with at least:
- state/county/township/municipality
- source agency/dataset/version/url
- source record ID
- source route/road identity ID (ODOT NLF, WVDOT ROUTE_ID, PennDOT LRS/SR/local ID as applicable)
- route class/type/number/suffix/fraction
- official/current street name
- alternate/911/legacy names when source-backed
- geometry
- jurisdiction/maintainer where available
- road class/surface/t

records.title: fix(core): prevent symlink cycles in SearchIndex::build
records.body:
## Problem

`SearchIndex::build` in `crates/cadis-core/src/search_index.rs:44-72` walks the workspace iteratively using `entry.metadata()` (which follows symlinks) with no canonicalization and no visited set. A symlink pointing to an ancestor directory re-pushes the same real directory forever. Issue #232 covers `search_files` in `tools.rs` only — verified against the issue body — not this index-build path.

## Actual Output

Any workspace containing a self-referential symlink (e.g. `ln -s . loop`) makes the first `file.search` (index built lazily at `lib.rs:4976-4979`) loop forever, consuming CPU/memory until the daemon is killed — a safe-read tool that needs no approval.

## How to Fix

Track canonicalized visited directories in a `HashSet` and/or add a depth cap during the index walk (mirroring the #232 fix), and add a unit test with a symlink-cycle fixture (Windows: junction).

## Expected Output

Index builds terminate on workspaces with symlink cycles; `file.search` returns results instead of hanging.

## Critical Level

Medium

## My Confidence

High

## Why Matters?

Availability: the same exploit family as #232 but through a different, unguarded code path that stays open after the #232 fix.

## Task


Please fix the hosted review workflow timeout status mismatch.

Context:

The hosted review workflow currently writes timeout results as `status: "timeout"`:

- `.github/workflows/herd-review.yml`
- `internal/cli/workflows/herd-review.yml.tmpl`

Specifically, when `timeout` exits with rc 124 or 137, the workflow creates `/tmp/herd-review-command-result.json` with:

```json
{"status":"timeout", "summary":"Herd Review timed out ..."}
```

The `Report review result` step also treats `timeout` as an allowed status in its shell `case` statement.

But the control-plane job result parser accepts `timed_out`, not `timeout`:

- `internal/controlplane/jobs/results.go` defines `StatusTimedOut = "timed_out"`
- `validReviewStatus` only accepts `timed_out`
- `internal/controlplane/review/reviews.go` also uses `ResultStatusTimedOut = "timed_out"`

Impact:

If the hosted review workflow times out, it posts a callback payload with `status: "timeout"`. The control plane rejects that as `invalid review result status "timeout"`, so Herd does not cleanly record the timed-out review result/status.

Required fix:

1. Change the hosted review workflow timeout result status from `timeout` to `timed_out` in both:
   - `.github/workflows/herd-review.yml`
   - `internal/cli/workflows/herd-review.yml.tmpl`

2. Change the `Report review result` shell allow-list from:

```sh
approved|changes_requested|failed|timeout|unparseable)
```

to include `timed_out` instead of `timeout`.

3. Add or update workflow rendering tests to assert:
   - timeout branches emit `--arg status "timed_out"`
   - the report status allow-list contains `timed_out`
   - the rendered template still matches the committed workflow

4. Add or update parser/handler tests if useful to prove `timed_out` is accepted and `timeout` remains rejected, unless that is already covered clearly.

Constraints:

- Keep this focused. Do not change unrelated hosted review behavior.
- Do not reintroduce `timeout` as an accepted alias unless there is a strong reason; the canonical status should be `timed_out`.
- Keep the generated workflow and committed workflow in sync.
- Run the focused tests for workflow rendering and job result parsing/handling.

---

  version: 1
  batch: 106
  type: fix
  fix_cycle: 59

---

## Task


The latest worker commit #1018 still leaves PR #849 failing CI and missed at least one production durability issue. Please fix these before continuing review cycles.

Current blocking CI failure:

- `go test ./... -count=1 -race` fails in `internal/controlplane/workflowevents`.
- Focused reproduction:

  `GOCACHE=/tmp/herd-go-cache go test ./internal/controlplane/workflowevents -race -count=1`

- Race details:
  - `internal/controlplane/workflowevents/handler_test.go:332` reads `processor.blockStarted` via `<-processor.blockStarted`.
  - `internal/controlplane/workflowevents/handler_test.go:681-683` writes `p.blockStarted = nil` inside `capturingProcessor.ProcessWorkflowEvent`.
  - Non-race test passes, but CI runs with `-race`, so this blocks the PR.

Required fix:

- Make `TestHandlerConcurrentDuplicateWorkflowEventProcessesOnce` race-clean.
- Do not remove the concurrency coverage. The test must still prove concurrent duplicate workflow events call `ProcessWorkflowEvent` exactly once.
- Prefer capturing the channel in a local variable before starting the goroutine, or adding a synchronized helper on `capturingProcessor`.
- Run and report:

  `GOCACHE=/tmp/herd-go-cache go test ./internal/controlplane/workflowevents -race -count=1`

Production durability issue still unfixed:

- `cmd/herd-service/dependencies.go:dispatchIssueCommand` still performs GitHub-visible issue label mutations directly before durable workflow dispatch is recorded:
  - removes the current status label
  - adds `herd/status:in-progress`
  - on dispatch failure, directly removes `in-progress` and adds `failed`

Why this is still a bug:

- If the service crashes or is cancelled after labels change but before durable dispatch completion, redelivery can see the issue as `in-progress` and reject it as `expected ready or failed`.
- That can wedge `@herd-os dispatch` with no worker actually running.
- This was one of the latest review findings and #1018 did not migrate this path.

Required fix:

- Route `@herd-os dispatch` issue status transitions through the same durable mutation/idempotency model used by hosted orchestration, or centralize issue status transitions in a shared durable helper.
- Do not perform direct `RemoveLabels` / `AddLabels` for production hosted dispatch state transitions without mutation records.
- Add a regression test simulating failure/crash after `in-progress` is applied but before dispatch completes, then redelivery should either dispatch exactly once or repair labels without losing the work.

Test coverage regression to fix:

- `internal/controlplane/commands/handler_test.go:571` is named `TestHandlerDispatchStatusAndFallbackFailureRedeliveryDoesNotDispatchAgain`, but it now asserts `dispatcher.dispatched` has length `2`.
- If the intended behavior is that the command handler may re-enter the dispatcher while the concrete dispatcher suppresses/replays the workflow dispatch idempotently, the test should model that explicitly.
- The test name and assertion currently contradict each other and weaken the guarantee.

Required fix:

- Either restore the stronger guarantee at the command-handler level, or update the fake dispatcher to model cpdispatch idempotent replay and assert exactly one underlying workflow dispatch is created.
- Do not leave a test named `DoesNotDispatchAgain` asserting two dispatch calls without proving no duplicate GitHub workflow dispatch side effect occurs.

Validation required before pushing:

- `GOCACHE=/tmp/herd-go-cache go test ./internal/controlplane/workflowevents -race -count=1`

records.title: modularui-3.1.5: getAllHovered()'s iterator recurses instead of ending, so exhausting it kills the client
records.body:
## Summary

`ModularGuiContext.getAllHovered()` in **modularui-3.1.5** returns an `Iterable` whose iterator
**never terminates**. Iterating it to the end — which any ordinary `for`-each does — recurses until
the stack dies. It killed the 365-jar client twice on 2026-08-24, once per hover probe.

This is **not conditional on our widget tree** and **not reachable by a player**. It is a plain
defect in the dependency, and we have a workaround plus a gate. This issue exists so the workaround
is revisited deliberately on a ModularUI bump instead of outliving its cause.

**Do not report this upstream from here.** Jake decides whether it goes to the ModularUI project.

## The defect, in bytecode

`getAllHovered()` returns the `hoveredIterable` field, a lambda-backed `Iterable` whose
`iterator()` is `lambda$new$0()`, which builds `ModularGuiContext$1` — a Guava `AbstractIterator`.
Its `computeNext()` disassembles to:

```
  computeNext()Lcom/cleanroommc/modularui/api/widget/IWidget;
        0: aload_0; getfield this$0; invokestatic ModularGuiContext.access$100  -> this.hovered
       11: if_acmpeq 24                       // hovered != currentHovered ?
       14: new java/util/ConcurrentModificationException ... athrow
       24: aload_0; getfield it; invokeinterface java/util/Iterator.hasNext()Z
       33: ifeq 57
       36: it.next(); checkcast LocatedWidget; getElement(); checkcast IWidget
       54: goto 61
       57: aload_0; invokevirtual ModularGuiContext$1.computeNext()   <-- ITSELF
       61: areturn
```

In source terms:

```java
return this.it.hasNext() ? this.it.next().getElement() : computeNext();   // line 71
```

The else branch calls **itself** where `AbstractIterator` requires `endOfData()`. The string
`endOfData` appears **nowhere in that class's constant pool**, so the iterator's state can never
reach `DONE`. `LineNumberTable` puts `pc=24` at line 71, which is why the crash is a wall of
identical frames at `ModularGuiContext.java:71`.

The sibling iterator `ModularGuiContext$HoveredIterable$1`, behind `getAllBelowMouse()`, **does**
call `endOfData()`. So this is one broken iterator, not a broken pattern — which also means
`getAllBelowMouse()` is safe to iterate and `getAllHovered()` is not.

Full disassembly, line table and both iterators:
`/coding/.recipegraph-build/evidence-tipfix/modulargui-iterator-bytecode.txt`

## Why a caller cannot defend itself

The overflow happens **inside the `hasNext()` that would have reported the end**. So there is no
loop shape that avoids it: a cap does not help, because the `hasNext()` after the last real element
is the one that recurses. The only safe uses are "break before the end on every possible input" —
which no honest probe can guarantee — or not calling it at all.

## How it reached us

Both hover screens added in #333 build a diagnostic log line from a walk of the whole set, so
neither could ever have completed one:

| screen | crashed | stack depth | Forge listener |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `planner-machine-tip` | 10:20:47 | 1024 frames at `ModularGuiContext.java:71` | Index 44, `ShotHarness$Runner.onRenderTick` |
| `planner-hover` | 18:46:14 | 1024 frames at `ModularGuiContext.java:71` | Index 44, `ShotHarness$Runner.onRenderTick` |

**Both screens recursed to an identical 1024-frame ceiling**, and that identity is the point:
1024 is the JVM's `MaxJavaStackTraceDepth`, not a property of our widget tree, and the same depth
reached by two different callers is what a defect *in the iterator* looks like. An earlier revision
of this issue gave 3072 for `planner-hover`, which was the whole-file count of `:71` lines rather
than a stack depth, and comparing it against the other screen's 1024 invented a difference that
does not exist. Each crash emits **three** stack dumps of exactly 1024 frames as the error
propagates — the caught `RenderTickEvent`, the unreported exception, and the crash report — so
3072 is three dumps, not one deep one. Caught in review by reviewer-tipfix.

`final-battery.log` is cumulative and now holds **both** episodes: eight `StackOverflowError`
markers in two groups of `{1024, 1024, 1024, 4}`, where the trailing 4 is LoliASM's own truncated
copy in the crash report. No third screen is affected — `flow-node-menu`, `planner-view-todo` and
`planner-caveats` all ran clean after both crashes.

Corroboration that the walk never once finished: `resolved=[`, the string that log line always
emits, appears **zero** times anywhere in `final-battery.log` (re-checked at 25 MB, after three
further screens were appended) and zero times in the `planner-hover` log.

`planner-hover` is the sharp one. `hoverVerdict` resolves no tooltip, touches no `Icon` and never
looks at the machine cell — it only wanted the diagnostic — and it died identically. That rules out
the tooltip, the icon and the widget tree in one measurement.

## Why no player can hit it

- **Not one of the 382 jars the client loads calls `getAllHovered()`.** Scanned every class in
  ev
